Answer: B
Reason: The serial chest X-rays (Figures 1a-1c) demonstrate a cystic lesion in the right lung that has increased in size over time, indicating slow growth since 1988. The linear opacity visible within the cyst (indicated by arrows in Figure 1b) represents a prominent intracystic vessel, which is characteristic of a dilated vein often seen in conditions like pulmonary varix or sequestration, rather than an artery or connective tissue cord.
